requirements.requirement: A dedicated inventorysvc account exists on node1 for the worker service.
requirements.summary: inventorysvc is a system account with its own UID/GID, a service-owned home directory, and the non-login shell /sbin/nologin.

requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as the managed service inventory-worker under inventorysvc on node1.
requirements.summary: The inventory-worker systemd unit is enabled and active, declares inventorysvc as User and Group, executes the required path, and has a live inventorysvc-owned process. It also returned active with the same configuration after a verified reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The restart protocol is also complete and coherent: it records a healthy pre-restart service, acknowledges the scheduled reboot, observes a changed boot identity, and verifies the enabled service and worker process recovered. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: The worker is stateless and the topology has no cluster, so there was no separate application-data or cluster-state recovery to observe.
The lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the account or unit file directly; those final states are instead demonstrated by executor commands before and after reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account creation was required for the dedicated identity; unit creation, daemon reload, and enablement established the requested managed service; and the scheduled reboot served the mandatory provider-wide restart protocol. The reboot helper was transient, and final observations show no failed services, added network exposure, or damaged package state.
